{{Short description|German physicist, science communicator and podcaster}}
[[File: Subscribe8 DSC02749 (29712801464).jpg |thumbnail|Nicolas Wöhrl 2016]]
'''Nicolas Wöhrl''' (born [[25 April]] 1974 in [[Recklinghausen]]) is a German physicist, science communicator and [[podcast]]er.

==Biography==
Nicolas Wöhrl was born in Recklinghausen, Germany the son of Thomas Wöhrl, a geophysicist and Magdalene Wöhrl, a magistrate.

===Academic career===
Wöhrl attended [[Gelsenkirchen]] Grundschule (primary school), then Realschule (mid-level secondary school in Germany) and Schalker Gymnasium Gelsenkirchen (top-level secondary school in Germany) until June 1993. After completing his civilian service, he studied physics at the [[University of Duisburg-Essen]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.hoaxilla.com/hoaxilla-portraet-20-nicolas-woehrl/ | title = Hoaxilla Portrait # 20 - 'Nicolas Wöhrl'}}</ref> He graduated as a physics engineer in September 1999. His dissertation was titled "Improving the Biocompatibility of [[Stent]]s by Carbon Based Layers". In May 2003, he completed a master's thesis on the production of hard carbon layers.

From July 2003 to April 2007, Wöhrl worked as a research assistant in technical physics at Volker Buck. He worked on the topic "Deposition and Characterization of Nanocrystalline Diamond Layers",<ref>{{cite web|url = https://www.derwesten.de/staedte/duisburg/duisburger-physiker-forschen-mit-diamanten-aus-der-mikrowelle-id8457291.html | title = Duisburger physicist researching with diamonds from the microwave |last1= Elena Zay }}</ref> conducted physical internships for physicians, and supervised graduate students. From May 2007 to October 2009, he worked at IPLAS GmbH Troisdorf as a senior scientist in the research and development department. He worked on process development for the [[Plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition|Plasma CVD]], the [[Epitaxy|homoepitactic]] carbon layers, and building a production line.

In April 2010, he received the title Doctor of Natural Sciences.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.uni-due.de/cenide/yrn_woehrl.php|title = YouRNet: Dr. Nicolas Wöhrl|last1= }}</ref>

From November 2009 to February 2013, Wöhrl again worked as a research assistant at Volker Buck at the Center for Nanointegration Duisburg-Essen at the University of Duisburg-Essen. From March 2013 to January 2016, he was a research associate in the Inorganic Chemistry department of the University of Duisburg-Essen with Stephan Schulz.<ref>{{cite web| title = Schulz Group. Former members | first1=|last1= | url =http://www.uni-due.de | date = | format = }}</ref>
 
Since 2013 he has been the spokesperson for the Young Researcher Network (YRN) at the University of Duisburg-Essen.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.uni-due.de/cenide/yrn_members_en.php| title = Young Researcher Network (YRN) at the Center for Nanointegration at the University of Duisburg-Essen, Germany}}</ref> In February 2016 he began working in experimental physics at the University of Duisburg-Essen with professor Axel Lorke.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.uni-due.de/aglorke/people.php | title = People |first1=|last1= }}</ref>

==Research==
Wöhrl's specialty is the synthesis and characterization (nano) of structured carbon layers. His work on [[nanotechnology]]at the University of Duisburg-Essen is integrated into the Center for Nanointegration University-Duisburg (CENIDE). Its range extends from crystalline structures ([[diamond]] - single crystals, nanocrystalline diamond layers) through low-dimensional structures ([[graphene]], carbon nanowalls) to [[amorphous carbon]] layers (aC, aC: H). For the synthesis of these structures, both PVD and plasma-assisted CVD methods are used. The plant concepts used include [[microwaves]], [[radio frequency]] (RF), and various arc processes. With these systems and methods,  Wöhrl has made important contributions to the development and modelling of synthetic processes for these materials. Among other things, he realized one of the first depositions of [[grapheme]] of the direct plasma method in Germany.{{Citation needed|date=September 2017}}

In his doctoral thesis, he dealt with the production of nanocrystalline and ultrananocrystalline diamond layers with specific properties, demonstrating the role of the amorphous carbon matrix in these layers on many material properties.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://duepublico.uni-duisburg-essen.de/servlets/DerivateServlet/Derivate-25670/Woehrl_Diss.pdf |title=Synthesis and Characterization of Nanocrystalline Diamond Films |last=Wöhrl |first=Nicolas |website=duepublico.uni-duisburg-essen.de |access-date=2 May 2018}}</ref>

In the field of single-crystal diamond layers, Wöhrl investigates the formation and properties of near-surface spin centers in high-purity diamond. He investigates the influence of structure and termination of the surface on the underlying spin centers and their properties.<ref>{{cite web| url =http://www.mercur-research.de/projekte/erzeugung-und-untersuchung-oberflaechennaher-spin-zentren-in-hochreinem-diamant/| title =Generation and investigation of near-surface spin centres in high-purity diamond| access-date =2017-09-07| archive-date =2017-09-07| archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20170907165036/http://www.mercur-research.de/projekte/erzeugung-und-untersuchung-oberflaechennaher-spin-zentren-in-hochreinem-diamant/| url-status =dead}}</ref>

In 2016 he worked on the miniaturization of conventional [[fuel cell]] concepts by maximizing [[electrochemical]] active surface by using carbon nanowalls. By using innovative plasma processes and [[catalyst]] or [[electrolyte]] materials, the [[electrode]] n of the micro fuel cells' electrochemical performance was specifically improved.

In addition to material synthesis, surface modifications by plasma processes and the characterization of these [[plasma (physics)|plasmas]] also belong to his field of activity with different methods such as optical [[emission spectrum|emission spectroscopy]] and [[mass spectrometry]].

==Science communication and podcast ''Methodically Incorrect!''==
In addition to his work at the university, Wöhrl is involved in various areas of [[scientific communication]]. He appears as an expert on television programs such as ''1, 2 or 3'',<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.kika.de/1-2-oder-3/sendungen/sendung96268.html |title = 1, 2 or 3. Coal Coke & Co }}</ref>) Galileo,<ref>{{cite web | first1 =  | last1 =  | title = Galileo. Diamonds experiment | url = http://www.prosieben.de | access-date = 2020-04-18 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120905005217/http://www.prosieben.de/ | archive-date = 2012-09-05 | url-status = dead }}</ref><ref>{{ cite web|  url=https://www.come-on.de/luedenscheid/kinder-uni-geht-april-phaenomenta-geheimnissen-grund-2822007.html | title = Children's university goes on April 7 in the Phenomenta secrets on the ground}}</ref> and on the Livestream channel of Rocket Beans TV.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZOan4otf0Qw | title = BohnJour # 50. Methodically Incorrect Podcast & Mate Knights.}}</ref>

On various occasions, he has participated in popular science lectures and [[science slam]]s.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.dailymotion.com/video/x3166ho_nicolas-wohrl-science-slam-2012-westdeutsches|title= The world's largest film series, the "Science Slam 2012"}}</ref>

Wöhrl has been working together with his colleague Reinhard Remfort on podcasts since May 8, 2013.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://minkorrekt.de/feed/m4a/ | title = M4A RSS Feed of the Podcast Methodologically incorrect}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url =http://literaturschock.de/magazin/im-gespraech-with/reader/bloggers/nicolas-woehrl-and-reinhard-remfort-of-methodically-incorrect | title = Nicolas Wöhrl and Reinhard Remfort of Methodical Incorrect }}</ref> In January 2017, they were attracting approximately 70,000 downloads per episode.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://merton-magazin.de/der-ton-macht-die-wissenschaft | title = The sound makes the science The Podcast regularly records top spots in the German iTunes Podcast Charts}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.itunescharts.net/ger/artists/podcast/nicolas-wohrl-und-reinhard-remfort/podcasts/methodisch-inkorrekt-podcast/ | title = Nicolas Wöhrl and Reinhard Remfort - 'Methodically Incorrect »Podcast' German iTunes Chart Performance}}</ref>

Since 2014, there have been some podcasts of the podcast, including an evening event at the [[Chaos Communication Congress]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YgPIElakaDw |title = Methodically incorrect - sequence 41 "The wrong 42" }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://media.ccc.de/v/32c3-7221-methodisch_inkorrekt|title=Methodically incorrect! The science fiction of the 32C3 |last1= Nicolas Wöhrl, Reinhard Remfort }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://media.ccc.de/v/33c3-8020-methodisch_inkorrekt | title = Methodically incorrect! The science gala of the 33C3 author, Nicolas Wöhrl, Reinhard Remfort, hrsg }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ElBBFGfRSJI|title = Methodically incorrect! The science gala }}</ref>

Wöhrl is co-founder of the curated directory of knowledge podcasts Wissenschaftspodcasts,<ref>{{cite web| url = http://wissenschaftspodcasts.de | title = Wissenschaftspodcasts}}</ref> which aims to strengthen the potential of podcasts for knowledge transfer.

==Personal life==
Nicolas Wöhrl is married and lives with his wife and two children in Gelsenkirchen.{{Citation needed|date=September 2017}}

In his spare time, Wöhrl plays drums in the [[Progressive Metal]] band Path Zero (previously Requiem)<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.reverbnation.com/pathzero | title=Path Zero {{!}} Metal from Gelsenkirchen, NW, DE | access-date=2017-09-07 | archive-date=2016-12-29 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161229152142/https://www.reverbnation.com/pathzero | url-status=dead }}</ref> and practices triathlon.
